title: Skybase must obtain per-grant governance consent for post-Genesis funding, while other Agents hold blanket transfer authorizations
content:
Two funding regimes sit side by side in this chunk. A.2.8.2.7.2.2.3 subjects Skybase's post-Genesis grant requests to the limitations in A.2.2.6.2.3.1 ("Limitations On Usage Of Root Edit Primitive Prior To Independent Governance") and requires that "Sky Governance must consent to the transfer of funds for each such grant via an Atlas Edit." The July 2026 grant of 700,000 USDS is duly recorded as an individually consented authorization (A.2.8.2.7.2.2.3.1), naming the destination multisig.

Against that, A.2.8.2.5.2.4, A.2.8.2.8.2.2 and A.2.8.2.9.2.2 give Core Council Executor Agent 1, Amatsu and Ozone standing authority to move Genesis Capital to the Sky Frontier Foundation "without a separate governance decision for each transfer."

The distinguishing variable is named in the cross-reference: independent governance. Skybase is a Star that has not yet established its own governance, so Sky retains transaction-level control over anything beyond the initial allocation. The Executor Agents are internal service providers whose destination is a Sky-side foundation, so per-transfer review adds process without adding protection.

The pattern to carry forward is that scrutiny is calibrated to *counterparty independence and destination*, not to amount — the 700,000 USDS grant needed an Atlas Edit while far larger Executor Agent transfers need none.
description: Skybase's follow-on grants each require an Atlas Edit under the Root Edit Primitive limitations;
